first_impression.reaction: My assistant sent it, so I looked at the first screen. 'Most ring guides rank settings by looks. This one asks what happens on a ski lift, a reef dive and a long-haul flight.' That's a good line, calm and not gushing. But this is a jeweller's question, not a planner's. My ring is being made by our family jeweller. I read the takeaways and the wedding section at the end and left the rest for my assistant.

journey.quote: Most ring guides rank settings by looks. This one asks what happens on a ski lift, a reef dive and a long-haul flight.
journey.reaction: Understated and sure of itself. Nothing cheap in the tone. It doesn't make me feel like a package customer.

journey.section: How to choose a ring setting when you live an active life
journey.quote: For the money side, see our guide to [how much to spend on an engagement ring](/expert-advice/how-much-should-you-spend-on-an-engagement-ring).
journey.reaction: A budget link on the first screen. Not a problem in itself, but it tells me who this was written for, and it isn't us.

journey.quote: Pack the ring in your carry-on, never checked luggage, and tell your insurer your travel dates.
journey.reaction: Sensible, but basic. For a family wedding abroad the real question is the jewellery for the whole family and the bridal party: who carries it, who holds it at the venue, who is responsible. Nothing on that.

journey.section: From the ring to the adventure: planning a wedding abroad
journey.quote: A ring chosen for the trail often comes with a wedding in the same spirit: a mountain lodge, a coastline, a long weekend that runs into the honeymoon.
journey.reaction: This is a small, relaxed wedding. Pleasant, but it says nothing about 300 guests, closing a property or working with our security. It confirms I'm not the reader.

journey.quote: Wedded Concierge plans venue, travel, vendors and payments anywhere in the world, with one Wedded Advisor as your single point of contact from start to finish.
journey.reaction: One senior contact anywhere in the world is the right promise for me. It just needs some sign you've delivered at our scale, and quietly.

unanswered_questions: Has Wedded Concierge handled weddings of 200 to 400 guests with VIP guests?
How do you handle security for valuables, including bridal and family jewellery, at a venue abroad, and do you work with a client's own security team?
Is there a private channel or direct line to someone senior, rather than a general enquiry form?
How is client discretion protected (staff, vendors, social media)?
would_share_with: No one. My assistant files it.

cta_reaction.quote: [Talk to a Wedded Concierge about a wedding abroad](/wonderland-concierge).
cta_reaction.why: Not from a ring care article. Nothing here tells me you've handled a wedding our size, and I don't enquire through a general link. My assistant might look at the concierge page later if someone we know mentions you.

top_3_changes: In the wedding-abroad section, don't describe only small weddings ('a long weekend that runs into the honeymoon'). One line saying the same team handles large family weddings and private logistics would keep readers like me on board.

In the travel section, add one sentence on keeping valuables secure at the wedding itself (who holds them, safe storage, working with the venue), if that can be sourced. That's the jewellery question families like mine actually ask.
Move the budget link out of the opening section and into the end or the FAQ, so the first screen reads as expert advice and not as spending guidance.
